info.name: HESCO Auth Service
info.description:
auth_policy_prompt.md's 5 endpoints, against feature/auth-module-fixes. Run the SETUP request's SQL manually against your DB first (see its description) - there's no seed data for a test account in the repo.

All requests use {{baseUrl}} = http://localhost:8084 by default (matches application.yml's server.port). {{token}} and {{resetToken}} are captured automatically by test scripts on Login and Forgot Password respectively - run requests in order top to bottom the first time.

item.name: 0. SETUP (read me - run this SQL first)

request.description:
This is not a real request to run - it's a placeholder for the one-time setup SQL, since the repo has no seed test user.

Run this against your DB once (adjust circle/division/subdivision if HESCO_ADMIN's SYSTEM_WIDE bound type requires it to stay NULL - check role.assigned_bound_type before inserting):

```sql
INSERT INTO app_user (username, password_hash, first_name, last_name, is_active, role_id)
SELECT 'hesco_admin', '$2b$12$GkaJzgkGSVoSvljtAbVUb.P1K/B5njzCsWNWTCfDOTE3YkIzdhuc.',
       'HESCO', 'Admin', true, r.id
FROM role r WHERE r.code = 'HESCO_ADMIN';
```

The hash above is a real BCrypt hash of `Passw0rd!123` (this collection's default {{password}} variable) - generated with the same plain-BCrypt scheme AuthService now expects everywhere, so login will work immediately without needing the legacy-plaintext-migration code path.

password_changed_at is left NULL on purpose - that's the "legacy/never tracked" state, so this account won't show as password-expired on first login. Log in once, then use Change Password to set password_changed_at and start the normal 30-day clock.

Sets {{token}} on success, used as the Bearer token by every other request below.

Expected 200 response shape:
```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "token": "...",
    "expiresAt": "...",
    "userId": 1,
    "username": "hesco_admin",
    "firstName": "HESCO",
    "lastName": "Admin",
    "roleCode": "HESCO_ADMIN",
    "boundType": "SYSTEM_WIDE",
    "circleId": null,
    "divisionId": null,
    "subDivisionId": null,
    "passwordExpired": false,
    "mustChangePassword": false,
    "passwordExpiresInDays": null
  },
  "message": null
}
```
`passwordExpiresInDays` is null here because the SETUP account has no password_changed_at yet (legacy/never-tracked state).

Confirms InvalidCredentialsException -> 401 via the shared GlobalExceptionHandler, and that a wrong password gets the SAME message as an unknown username (no user enumeration). Also writes a FAILURE row to login_history - check via request 6 afterward.

Requires a valid Bearer token (identity comes from the JWT, not the request body). On success: archives the OLD hash to password_history, sets password_changed_at (starts the 30-day clock), clears mustChangePassword, and writes a SELF_SERVICE password_change_audit row.

After running this once, {{password}} in this collection is stale - either update the collection variable to {{newPassword}}'s value before re-running Login, or use request 2b to see the policy/reuse rejections instead.

Demonstrates PasswordPolicyViolationException -> 400 (too short, missing upper/digit/special). Change newPassword to {{newPassword}}'s current value instead to demonstrate PasswordReuseException -> 400 (new password == current password) - both return the shared ApiErrorResponse shape.

Public endpoint - no Bearer token needed (a user resetting a forgotten password doesn't have one). Sets {{resetToken}} for request 4.

devOnlyRawToken is a DEV/DEMO placeholder - see ForgotPasswordResponse's javadoc. In any real deployment this must be emailed/SMS'd, not returned in the API response; the same request against an unknown username returns an identical shape with a null token, so this endpoint can't be used to enumerate valid usernames.

item.name: 3b. Forgot Password (rate limit - run 4x fast for 429)

request.description: Use Postman's Runner to fire this 4 times in under an hour - the 4th should come back 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS (RateLimitExceededException), enforcing the 3/hour cap from auth_policy_prompt.md §4.

Public endpoint. Consumes {{resetToken}} from request 3 - tokens are single-use (used_at gets set) and expire after 15 minutes, so re-running this without a fresh Forgot Password call first will return 400 (InvalidResetTokenException - the same message whether the token was never valid, already used, or expired, so it can't be used to probe token existence).

On success: same applyNewPassword path as Change Password, but change_type is FORCED_RESET in password_change_audit instead of SELF_SERVICE, and no old password is required.

Requires a valid Bearer token - returns the CALLER's own history only (identity from the JWT), most recent first, capped at 50 rows. Run request 1b (wrong password) first to see a FAILURE entry alongside the SUCCESS ones - note {{token}} has to be a currently-valid token from a successful login, so run this AFTER re-logging-in if you've since changed the password.
